analysis.hypothesis: The existing custom_ops.cu defines CUDA kernels and extern "C" launcher functions for cat_forward, prod_forward, and cat_prod_forward. The missing binding file must provide PyTorch wrappers that validate inputs, allocate outputs, copy shape/stride metadata to device, launch kernels on the current CUDA stream, and register Python functions with pybind. The .cu launchers expect shape/stride arrays as device pointers because kernels dereference them on GPU. Thus the binding must allocate device memory for metadata using cudaMalloc/cudaMemcpyAsync, pass these device pointers to the launchers, and free them after kernel completion (or use a temporary allocation). All tensors must be float32 CUDA tensors. The dim parameter is int64_t in C++ and passed as int to launcher after checking range. For cat_forward, output shape is computed by concatenating dimensions; for prod_forward and cat_prod_forward, output shape removes the reduction dimension. The kernels support arbitrary strides, so no contiguous requirement is necessary, but the output is always contiguous. The binding must include torch/types.h, torch/csrc/utils/pybind.h, cuda_runtime.h, c10/cuda/CUDAStream.h, and binding_registry.h. We will use the exact external function declarations matching the .cu file. No torch operations are used for computation; only PyTorch tensor allocation and metadata extraction.
